patch.value: Four more fail modes in the canonical gate: an arm pattern read as an opener, an escaped run key read as data, a sequence marker missing from the indent, and composite actions unscanned

The twelfth through fifteenth fail modes found in this gate, all reported by review on this branch and all confirmed by executing the auditor.

An arm pattern carrying the optional leading parenthesis was consumed as a balanced group, so the scan found the nested block's arm label instead of the enclosing one and skipped the sibling reset. A publish in the nested block then inherited the previous arm's binding. Two reviewers reported this independently; only the parenthesised spelling reproduced, because the bare spelling was already refused by another path.

A double-quoted YAML key carrying an escape was compared to the word run as raw text, so an escaped spelling of run was classified as data and its body never reached the shell scan. In isolation that merely made the scan vacuous, which fails closed. Composed with a single attested sibling the same construction returned no failures at all, which is the shape this gate keeps failing in and the reason a finding must be judged composed rather than alone.

The block scalar indentation indicator counts from the parent node, and in a sequence entry the item marker is part of that node's indentation. Omitting its width stripped two columns too few and left residual indentation, which is enough to stop a heredoc terminator matching at the shell line start. Settled against a real YAML parser rather than argued from the specification, which also showed that the existing guard for this construction was asserting against a document no parser accepts.

A composite action is recognised by its file name wherever it sits, so a repository that is itself an action carries the definition at its root. Matching only the actions subdirectory left those shell blocks unscanned.

An arm pattern written with or without its optional parenthesis resets the sibling scope; an escaped run key stays executable and a non-run key stays data whatever its spelling; a sequence entry's marker counts toward the indentation an indicator measures from, proven against a real YAML parser; a composite action at any path is scanned

All four confirmed by execution and fixed, with fourteen constructions re-verified and no regression. The escaped-key and arm-pattern guards are revert-proof against their own reverts. The opener refinement that distinguishes the case keyword from an arm pattern spelling it is pinned at unit level but had no end-to-end construction demonstrating a fail-open, and is recorded as a correctness refinement rather than a closed hole.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text:
A twelfth construction, found after the previous round and worth recording because it closes the loop on two earlier decisions.

Greptile reported that an arm pattern whose text reads like an opener suppresses the sibling reset. Its example used a quoted pattern, which does not reproduce, because quoted text is stripped before the scan. The unquoted grouped form does reproduce: an arm pattern of the shape open-paren, the word case, the word in, close-paren, followed by a nested case in the same segment, returned no failures for a publish the shell runs unattested.

This is the same construction the opener refinement removed in the previous commit would have caught, and that refinement was removed because CodeQL flagged it as a high-severity polynomial expression. So the two findings were in tension, and resolving them by tightening the expression again would have reintroduced the defect.

The predicate is rewritten instead. It asks a single anchored question: does the segment BEGIN with the case keyword followed by whitespace. That is one bounded quantifier with a literal between it and the next, so there is no adjacency to backtrack over. Everything else carrying an arm label is treated as a sibling, including a parenthesised pattern whose contents read like an opener. Deciding by position inside such a pattern is guesswork; treating it as a sibling is the fail-closed direction, because the only consequence of resetting is that a binding stops being visible.

Twelve constructions verified by execution with no regression.
